ravi (FinOps): Quick note — I've put together a short proposal for an 'interruption insurance' rate + ops buffer for preemptible GPU pools. Wanted reactions before we bake into chargeback tables.

ravi (FinOps): TL;DR: propose a 10% interruption insurance (applied to spot line items) + 3% ops buffer to cover manual recovery and reserve capacity. Net uplift ~13% on existing spot unit rates.

ravi (FinOps): Rationale: measured interruption_prob ~0.16 (weighted across regions), mean downtime per interruption ~1.2h, on-demand delta = $0.95/hr vs spot $0.28/hr for A100-like instances. Simple expected cost of interruption per spot-hour = 0.16 * (0.95 - 0.28) * 1.2 ≈ $0.13/hr -> ~46% of spot price. We smoothed that into a fixed 10% tax + ops buffer instead of pass-through billing volatility.

ravi (FinOps): sample calc block:
```
spot_price = 0.28
on_demand = 0.95
interrupt_prob = 0.16
mean_recovery_hours = 1.2
expected_interrupt_cost_per_spot_hour = interrupt_prob * (on_demand - spot) * mean_recovery_hours
# = 0.16 * 0.67 * 1.2 = 0.12864 
```

anya (Infra Eng): This is helpful. Two quick infra notes: 1) interruption_prob varies a lot by AZ and region (us-west2 spikes to ~0.25 vs eu-west1 ~0.08) so a single % will under/overcharge some teams. 2) we can reduce mean_recovery_hours by improving autoscaler and preemption-aware checkpointing.

jesse (SRE): +1 on separating ops buffer. Ops work (manual restarts, troubleshooting, warmup waste) is real and often non-linear. Suggest ops buffer be a fixed pool credit (3% sounds reasonable) that teams draw from; track usage and reconcile quarterly.

sam (EngOps): If we go with a flat insurance rate, can we make it adjustable by region? Proposal: base 10% global, with regional modifier: +5% for high-interruption regions, -3% for low. We should run this as experiment for 1 billing cycle.

maria (Product): From product/customer-facing POV: keep invoices simple. Show "Spot usage" and a single line "Interruption insurance + ops reserve (13%)" with a link to an explainer doc. Transparency avoids surprise.

anya (Infra Eng): Also want to call out mixed-capacity pools: many customers already use mixed on-demand+spot with internal hedging. For those, effective interruption exposure is lower and we should exclude them from the insurance or apply discounted rate. Need a detection rule: if a route has >=25% on-demand capacity pinned, mark as hedged.

ravi (FinOps): Good catch. I'll add a rule: if pinned on-demand >=25% for the route in the billing window, insurance rate = 0 (they already pay premium). If mixed but <25%, apply 50% of insurance.

ops-bot: autoscaler/smoothing-job completed: evaluated 48 clusters; predicted reduction in mean_recovery_hours = 20% if we deploy preemption hooks (https://internal/runbooks/preempt-hooks).

jesse (SRE): That's promising. If mean_recovery_hours drops to ~1.0, expected_interrupt_cost falls to ~0.107/hr and our flat insurance becomes more conservative. Keep tracking.

ravi (FinOps): Next steps I'm proposing:
- Run a one-cycle pilot (next billing month) with: insurance 10%, ops buffer 3%, regional modifiers applied, hedged-route exemption rules.
- Generate daily reconciliation export: route_id, billed_spot_hours, insurance_charged, hedged_flag.
- Quarterly true-up where we compare insurance collected vs actual interruption-related costs and adjust rate.

sam (EngOps): I can wire up the export in billing pipeline. Will need route_id schema and sampling for early access teams.

maria (Product): Create a short FAQ page for customers and a PR for billing docs. I can draft the phrasing.

anya (Infra Eng): We'll prioritize preempt-hook rollout to the top 20 clusters to reduce recovery time. ETA 2 weeks.

ravi (FinOps): ok, last ask: please react with :+1: if you approve pilot or comment if you want changes. If no objections by EOD Friday I'll timestamp the pilot start to the next billing cycle.

jesse (SRE): +1

sam (EngOps): +1

anya (Infra Eng): +1 (but will follow-up on regional modifiers PR)

maria (Product): +1

ravi (FinOps): Thanks all — will draft the billing change PR and post the pilot details next week.
